fixes.title: Pastes containing a web image inserted nothing at all
fixes.problem: Pasting content that included a web-hosted image inserted nothing. This happened with a web article with a photo, editor content with an uploaded image, or a table or list containing an image. The text, links, tables and the image were all silently lost.
fixes.cause: The `summernote.paste` handler returned early whenever `/]+src=["']https?:\/\//i` matched the clipboard HTML. Its comment said `onImageUpload` would handle the image, but that callback only fires for image files, never for `` tags in HTML. `preventDefault()` had already been called, so nothing was inserted.
fixes.change: Removes the early return. The whole paste now goes through `buildInsertNodes`/`cleanHtml`, which keeps loadable http(s) and `data:` images and the content around them.

image manipulation › images nested inside pasted tables and lists are retained
mixed-content pastes › web article with image: text before and after the image, list and link all retained
mixed-content pastes › image directly before a table, table trailing: both retained, caret below the table
mixed-content pastes › multiple tables and images in one paste: all retained in document order
RTE to RTE copy/paste › content containing an uploaded (https) image pastes fully — text and image
web page paste › article containing an https image pastes fully — text, link and image
fixes.shot: mixed-content pastes › web article with image: text before and after the image, list and link all retained

fixes.title: Pastes with embedded base64 images never saved to Appian
fixes.problem: Content whose images were embedded inline, such as modern Word or copied editor content, displayed correctly after pasting but was never saved. The save waited forever.
fixes.cause: `onImageUpload` only fires for clipboard image files, so `data:` images inside pasted HTML never went through `uploadBase64Img`. `setAppianValue` refuses to save while base64 content exists, so the value was never saved.
fixes.change: After insertion, the paste handler scans `.note-editable` for images where `isImageNewBase64` is true. This only runs when `window.connectedSystem` is set. Each image gets the `loading` class and is uploaded with `uploadBase64Img`. When the upload resolves, the returned document URL replaces the `src` and `setAppianValue` runs. Images that are already uploading are skipped, so nothing uploads twice.
tests: mixed-content pastes › Word section with text, embedded image, list and table SAVES to Appian
image manipulation › base64 image in pasted HTML: save waits for the upload, then goes through
RTE to RTE copy/paste › base64 image embedded in copied RTE content is retained and uploaded
paste robustness › pasting text while an image upload is in flight: both survive, save settles once
fixes.shot: mixed-content pastes › Word section with text, embedded image, list and table SAVES to Appian

fixes.title: Multi-line plain text pasted as one fused line
fixes.problem: Pasting plain text from Notepad, a terminal or a PDF viewer joined every line into one run of text. Bulleted lists and paragraphs from PDFs lost their line breaks, and the caret ended up in the wrong place.
fixes.cause:
A text-only clipboard reached `DOMParser` as a single text node, so its newlines collapsed into spaces. Converting the text to text plus `
` nodes and inserting them one by one does not work either: per the commit history, Summernote's `insertNode` misplaces the caret after a bare `
`.
fixes.change:
When the clipboard content does not start with `<`, the handler runs `cleanHtml(clipboardHtml, true)`. The raw-text branch of that function turns newlines into `
`. If the result contains `
`, it is wrapped in a single `

` so it is inserted as one block. Single-line text stays unwrapped and is inserted inline, so it does not split the paragraph it is pasted into.

paste at cursor position › multi-line plain text pasted mid-paragraph: following text pushed below, caret before it
RTE to RTE copy/paste › plain-text paste converts newlines to line breaks
PDF paste › multi-paragraph text: all paragraphs retained with line breaks
PDF paste › bulleted list: bullet glyphs and every item retained on separate lines
fixes.shot: PDF paste › bulleted list: bullet glyphs and every item retained on separate lines

fixes.title: Pasted HTML lost every block after the first
fixes.problem: When the copied HTML had line breaks or spaces between its paragraphs and headings, only the first block was pasted. Everything after it was silently dropped. Spaces between inline elements were also lost.
fixes.cause: In the inline paste loop, whitespace-only text nodes were dropped while cleaning (`node.textContent.trim()`). After the cleaned HTML was parsed again, any whitespace text nodes left next to block elements were passed to `insertNode`, which then lost the blocks that followed. The `trim()` check also dropped real spaces between inline elements.
fixes.change: The new `buildInsertNodes` keeps every text node while cleaning, so spaces between inline elements survive. After the second parse, it filters out whitespace-only text nodes next to a block element (`isBlockElement`/`BLOCK_LEVEL_REGEX`). Removing those nodes keeps `insertNode` from losing later blocks. A code comment records that the looser between-two-blocks rule was tried in a browser and failed.

fixes.title: Code blocks from web pages pasted as a single line
fixes.problem: Pasting a preformatted code block from a web page fused its lines together, and lines after the first could be lost.
fixes.cause:
`
` is not an allowed tag, so it is removed while its text stays. Upstream turned the newlines inside it into `
`, which left a bare run of text and `
` nodes at the top level. Per the commit history, `insertNode` loses the lines after the first in that situation.
fixes.change:
In the HTML-paste branch of `cleanHtml`, newlines inside each `
` block are converted to `
` and the block is wrapped in `
`. This happens before all other newlines are turned into spaces, so the lines stay separate and the code is inserted as one block.

fixes.shot: web page paste › code block: line breaks inside <pre> content are preserved

fixes.title: Script and style contents leaked into the editor as text
fixes.problem: Pasted HTML that contained a script (or style, iframe and similar tags) left the code visible in the editor as text, for example `window.__pwned = true;`. Content after the script could also be lost.
fixes.cause: Step 2 of `cleanHtml` only removed tags that were not on the allowlist and kept their inner text, so the contents of `<script>` and `<style>` stayed behind as text.
fixes.change: `cleanHtml` has a new Step 0. It uses `DANGEROUS_TAGS_PATTERN` to remove matched `script`, `style`, `iframe`, `object`, `embed` and `noscript` tags together with their contents. It then removes any remaining lone opening or self-closing forms of those tags with `DANGEROUS_TAGS_SELF_CLOSING_PATTERN`.
tests: paste sanitization › script tags are removed with their contents and never execute
fixes.shot: paste sanitization › script tags are removed with their contents and never execute

fixes.title: Broken temp-file and relative image references saved from pastes
fixes.problem: Images pasted from Word or Excel arrived as `file:///…clip_image` references to a temp file on the copier's machine. Relative image URLs were also kept. Both were saved to Appian as permanently broken images.
fixes.cause: `cleanHtml` kept any `` that passed the tag allowlist, whatever its `src`.
fixes.change: `cleanHtml` has a new Step 6.5 that only runs at paste time (`isPartialHtml`). It removes any `` whose `src` does not start with `http(s):` or `data:`, which includes images with no `src`. Content that is already stored is not affected.

web page paste › relative image URL in pasted HTML is dropped, surrounding text kept
Excel paste › range copied with an embedded chart: table retained, dead temp-file image dropped
fixes.shot: MS Word paste › embedded image: surrounding text retained; dead file:/// reference does not reach Appian

fixes.title: Images pasted twice or tables pasted with a picture of themselves
fixes.problem: Copying an image from a PDF viewer or web page inserted it twice. Excel and Word range copies inserted the table plus a bitmap snapshot of it. An Outlook copy produced two images.
fixes.cause: Summernote's own clipboard handling inserted every clipboard image file through `onImageUpload`, and the paste handler inserted the HTML version as well. Nothing decided whether the file was the content itself or a redundant snapshot of it.
fixes.change: Turns off Summernote's file insertion (`allowClipboardImagePasting: false`) and makes the paste handler the only place this is decided. If the HTML has no visible text, the image files are inserted with `insertImagesOrCallback` and the handler stops. If the HTML has text plus an image that cannot load (`UNLOADABLE_IMG_REGEX`, for example Outlook's `cid:`), the files are inserted and the text is pasted as well. Otherwise the HTML already carries the content and the files are ignored.

fixes.shot: redundant clipboard image files › Excel range copied with its bitmap snapshot: table pastes once, no picture-of-table

fixes.title: Copied non-image files inserted as broken images
fixes.problem: Pasting a file copied in the file explorer, such as a PDF, inserted a broken image with a `data:application/pdf` source and uploaded it. When both a PDF and an image were on the clipboard, both were inserted.
fixes.cause: Every clipboard file was read through `FileReader` and inserted as an ``, whatever its type.
fixes.change: The paste handler keeps only files whose type matches `/^image\//i` (`clipboardImageFiles`) before deciding whether to insert them. Files of any other type are ignored.

fixes.shot: clipboard edge cases › non-image FILE on the clipboard (a copied PDF document): nothing is inserted

fixes.title: Screenshots could be pasted when images were disabled
fixes.problem: With `allowImages` set to false, pasting a screenshot still inserted and uploaded the image.
fixes.cause: `allowImages` only controlled the toolbar picture button and HTML paste cleaning. Image files still reached the `onImageUpload` callback.
fixes.change: `onImageUpload` now returns right away when `window.allowImages` is false, so every way of adding an image respects the setting.
tests: image manipulation › screenshot paste is blocked when allowImages is false
fixes.shot: image manipulation › screenshot paste is blocked when allowImages is false

fixes.title: Content after a pasted table landed inside the table
fixes.problem: When a paste had a table followed by inline content such as an image or text, that content ended up inside the table's last cell instead of below it, which broke document order.
fixes.cause: `insertNode` leaves the caret inside the last cell of a newly inserted table. Per the code comment, a range placed after the table is normalized back into that cell, and `insertNode` reads Summernote's `lastRange` rather than the live selection.
fixes.change: In the insert loop, when a table is followed by a node that is not a block element, the handler reuses the empty paragraph after the table or creates one. It puts the caret at offset 0 of that paragraph and calls `editor.setLastRange` before inserting the next node.
code: `summernote.paste` handler (insert loop, caret placement after a table)

fixes.shot: mixed-content pastes › table pasted INTO existing text with an image following it keeps document order

fixes.title: Extra blank line and misplaced caret after a pasted table
fixes.problem: Pasting a table in the middle of existing text left two blank lines before the text that followed. After a trailing table, the caret looked stuck at the table's edge instead of on the blank line below it.
fixes.cause:
Upstream always inserted a new `


` after a trailing table, even when splitting the paragraph had already left an empty one there. It also left the selection after the `
`, a position the browser draws against the table's edge.
fixes.change:
The trailing-table block reuses `lastNode.nextSibling` when `isEmptyParagraph` is true for it, and only creates a new paragraph otherwise. It then collapses the selection to offset 0 of that paragraph, before the `
`.

RTE to RTE copy/paste › caret lands on the blank line below a pasted table, ready to type
fixes.shot: paste at cursor position › table pasted mid-content leaves exactly one blank line before the following text

fixes.title: Word pastes gained extra line breaks
fixes.problem: In text pasted from Word, the line breaks in Word's source HTML became visible breaks. A sentence made of several inline pieces was split across lines, and a Shift+Enter hard return produced two breaks.
fixes.cause:
The HTML-paste branch of `cleanHtml` turned every remaining `\n` into `
`, treating source-formatting newlines as real line breaks.
fixes.change:
In clipboard HTML, CR, LF and CRLF now become a space. Real line breaks come only from tags such as `
` and `

`; content inside `

` is the one exception. The regex that removed whitespace between tags is gone. The Word list-marker cleanup now strips any CR/LF run (`[\r\n]+`).

MS Word paste › hard returns (Shift+Enter) become a single
, not extra paragraphs

fixes.title: Stray empty paragraphs left behind after pasting
fixes.problem: Pressing Enter and then pasting left a stray blank line where the caret had been. Each repeated paste added another empty paragraph at the end of the document.
fixes.cause:
Upstream did not clean up the empty `

` at the caret or the new trailing empty paragraphs that `insertNode` leaves behind.
fixes.change: Before inserting, the handler records the empty caret paragraph (`findCaretEmptyParagraph`) and the blank paragraphs already at the end of the editor (`snapshotTrailingEmptyParagraphs`). After inserting, `removePasteArtifacts` removes the caret paragraph if it is still blank and has no image, table or list. It also removes trailing empty paragraphs that were not in the snapshot.

paste empty-paragraph cleanup › repeated pastes do not accumulate trailing empty paragraphs
fixes.shot: paste empty-paragraph cleanup › repeated pastes do not accumulate trailing empty paragraphs

fixes.title: Strikethrough from web pages was lost on paste
fixes.problem: Strikethrough copied from modern web pages or from the editor in the `<s>` form pasted as plain text.
fixes.cause: `ALLOWED_TAGS` contained the legacy `strike` but not `s`, so `cleanHtml` removed `<s>` tags.

fixes.title: Content-too-big error flashed while an image uploaded
fixes.problem: The maximum size error appeared during every image upload and disappeared once the upload finished.
fixes.cause: `validate` measured `getEditorContents().length`, which included the uploading image's large base64 data URI, even though that data is never saved.
fixes.change: `validate` replaces `src="data:…"` and `src='data:…'` values with `src=""` before comparing against `maxSize`. The size is still only computed when `!isReadOnly()` is true, because `getEditorContents` throws in read-only mode.
tests: editor lifecycle › maxSize validation does not flash while an image uploads

fixes.title: Unquoted and single-quoted attributes bypassed the attribute allowlist
fixes.problem: Attributes in Word HTML without quotes, such as `border=1` or `cellspacing=0`, were not filtered by the attribute allowlist. Style values in single quotes were also not filtered.
fixes.cause: The Step 3 regex in `cleanHtml`, `([\w-]+)="[^"]+?"`, only matched values in double quotes. The Step 4 style regex only looked ahead for `"`.
fixes.change: The Step 3 regex now matches values in double quotes, single quotes or no quotes, and Step 4's lookahead accepts either quote character. Step 7's comment regex now also matches comments that span several lines (`<!--[\s\S]*?-->`).

otherChanges: Moved the inline paste logic into named helpers (`buildInsertNodes`, `isBlockElement`, `hasBlankText`, `isEmptyParagraph`, `findCaretEmptyParagraph`, `snapshotTrailingEmptyParagraphs`, `removePasteArtifacts`), and moved `BLOCK_LEVEL_REGEX` and the dangerous-tag regexes to module-level constants.

Updated unit tests in `cleanHtml.test.js`, `cleanHtml.pasteEnhancements.test.js` and `pasteHandling.test.js` to match the new behavior: newlines in clipboard HTML become spaces, script/style contents are stripped, `<s>` is kept, and the attribute-regex edge case result changed.
Added the unit test file `cleanHtml.imageSources.test.js`, covering removal of `file:///`, missing-`src` and `javascript:` image sources.
Added the handler-level unit test file `pastePlainTextLineBreaks.test.js`, covering plain-text line breaks, whitespace filtering, `<pre>`, base64 upload and the clipboard-file decision.
Rewrote comments and applied Prettier formatting to `index.js` and the test files.
